chapter: Carnivals, Kansas City and the road to Chicago
title: Minstrel show tour: meeting George and Julia Lee and Herschel Evans
summary: Touring Iowa, Kansas, Arkansas and Texas with the show, he sat in with George and Julia Lee, turned down an Army band offer and still could not read music. In San Antonio he met the young Herschel Evans.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well, we traveled all through Iowa and then we went down into Kansas, and we went to -- in fact, when we were in Leavenworth, Kansas I met George Lee who was a band out of orchestra and Kansas City and he was with his sister, Julia Lee. And I went out that night and set in with them. Then I met a fellow in the Army whose name was Sawyer. And He wanted me to join the Army Sawyer was a saxophone player in the Army band. And, you know, I was a jazz man. I didn't know how to play anything else.
Had you learned to read by this time?

Not yet. Because everything I played was just off the top of my head. I didn't know anything about harmony or chords or anything. But everywhere I played everybody thought I was a great jazz man. In those days, you know,

jazz hadn't developed really gotten to the place where it is today. So every town I went to -- every chance I had to play extra, go out and jam or something, I did. Sawyer wanted me to join the Army out there and get in the Army band. It was a three year stretch and I said, no, I didn't want to get hung up. I stayed with the carnival, we traveled all down through Kansas and Arkansas and Texas. That year is the year I went to San Antonio and I met Herschel Evans. He was a kid.
Yeah, playing with a local band?
